subject: maths
title: Converting Units
seo_title: Year 4 Converting Units Worksheets: Length, Mass, Capacity and Time (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Convert between different units of measure [for example, kilometre to metre; hour to minute]; solve problems involving converting from hours to minutes; minutes to seconds; years to months; weeks to days.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on converting units: mm, cm, m and km, g and kg, ml and l, and seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years. Scales, jugs, comparing and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply. Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide.
key_sub: 1 km = 1,000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 l = 1,000 ml, but 1 hour = 60 minutes (not 100). So 3 km = 3,000 m and 180 minutes = 3 hours.
body_html:
Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply

A kilometre is much longer than a metre, so you need more metres to make the same distance. To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, multiply. To change a smaller unit into a bigger unit, divide.

Kilometres to metres

3 km = ☐ m

1 km = 1,000 m. Multiply: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000.

Answer: 3,000 m

Millilitres to litres

6,000 ml = ☐ l

1 l = 1,000 ml. Divide: 6,000 ÷ 1,000 = 6.

Answer: 6 l

Facts to know

MeasureFacts
Length1 cm = 10 mm   1 m = 100 cm   1 km = 1,000 m
Mass1 kg = 1,000 g
Capacity1 l = 1,000 ml
Time1 minute = 60 seconds   1 hour = 60 minutes   1 day = 24 hours
Longer times1 week = 7 days   1 year = 12 months   1 year = 365 days (366 in a leap year)

Two units together

Change the bigger unit first, then add what is left over. Watch the place value.

Kilograms and grams

2 kg 30 g = ☐ g

2 kg = 2,000 g. Add 30: 2,000 + 30 = 2,030.

Answer: 2,030 g

Hours and minutes

150 minutes = ☐ hours ☐ minutes

2 hours = 120 minutes. 150 − 120 = 30 minutes left over.

Answer: 2 hours 30 minutes

Read the scale, then convert

Halves and decimals

12 km = 500 m, 14 kg = 250 g and 1.5 l = 1,500 ml. To compare, change both to the same unit: 1,200 m is longer than 1 km 50 m, because 1 km 50 m = 1,050 m.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
1 hour = 100 minutes1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds
1 km = 100 m, or 1 m = 1,000 cm1 km = 1,000 m and 1 m = 100 cm
2 kg 30 g = 230 g2 kg = 2,000 g, so 2 kg 30 g = 2,030 g
Multiplying to get a bigger unit (8,000 m = 8,000,000 km)Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide (8,000 m = 8 km)
Comparing only the numbers (1,200 m < 1 km 50 m)Use one unit first: 1 km 50 m = 1,050 m, and 1,200 > 1,050

faq.q: What units do Year 4 children need to convert?
faq.a: The National Curriculum asks Year 4 pupils to convert between units such as kilometres and metres, metres and centimetres, kilograms and grams, litres and millilitres, and hours and minutes, minutes and seconds, years and months, and weeks and days.

faq.q: How do you convert kilometres to metres?
faq.a: Multiply by 1,000, because 1 km = 1,000 m. For example, 3 km = 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 m. To go back from metres to kilometres, divide by 1,000.
Time does not use tens like metric units: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds. So 150 minutes is 2 hours 30 minutes, not 1 hour 50 minutes.

faq.q: What is an easy way to remember metric conversions?
faq.a: Kilo means 1,000 (1 km = 1,000 m, 1 kg = 1,000 g), centi means a hundredth (1 m = 100 cm) and milli means a thousandth (1 l = 1,000 ml, 1 m = 1,000 mm). A ruler shows that 1 cm = 10 mm.

sets.title: Length: mm, cm, m and km

items.q: How many millimetres are in 1 centimetre?
items.e: Look at a ruler: there are 10 small marks in each centimetre. 1 cm = 10 mm.

items.q: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
items.e: Centi means one hundredth, so 1 m = 100 cm. A metre stick has 100 cm marked on it.

items.q: How many metres are in 1 kilometre?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 km = 1,000 m (not 100 m).

items.q: About how thick is a £1 coin?
items.e: A £1 coin is very thin, about 3 millimetres. 3 cm is even more than the width of the whole coin.

items.q: About how tall is a classroom door?
items.e: A door is a little taller than a grown-up, about 2 metres. 2 cm is shorter than your finger.

items.q: Pupils walk for about 15 minutes. About how far do they go?
items.e: In 15 minutes you can walk about 1 kilometre (1,000 m). 1 m is just one big step.

items.q: Convert. 6 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so you need more millimetres: multiply. 6 × 10 = 60, so 6 cm = 60 mm.

items.q: Convert. 7 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so you need more centimetres: multiply. 7 × 100 = 700, so 7 m = 700 cm.

items.q: Convert. 4 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so you need more metres: multiply. 4 × 1,000 = 4,000, so 4 km = 4,000 m.

items.q: Convert. 90 mm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so you need fewer centimetres: divide. 90 ÷ 10 = 9, so 90 mm = 9 cm.

items.q: Convert. 800 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so you need fewer metres: divide. 800 ÷ 100 = 8, so 800 cm = 8 m.

items.q: Convert. 9,000 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so you need fewer kilometres: divide. 9,000 ÷ 1,000 = 9, so 9,000 m = 9 km.

items.q: Convert. 12 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so you need more metres: multiply. 12 × 1,000 = 12,000, so 12 km = 12,000 m.
The pencil ends 4 small marks after 6 cm, so it is 6 cm 4 mm long. 1 cm = 10 mm, so 6 × 10 = 60, and 60 + 4 = 64 mm.
The pencil reaches 5 whole centimetres and then 7 small marks. Each small mark is 1 mm, so it is 5 cm 7 mm long (57 mm).
The pencil starts at 1 cm, not at 0. It ends at 8 cm 3 mm = 83 mm. Take away the start: 83 − 10 = 73 mm.

items.q: Convert. 3 m 5 cm = ☐ cm
items.e: 3 m = 300 cm. Add the 5 cm: 300 + 5 = 305 cm. Writing 35 cm forgets that 3 m is 300 cm.

items.q: Convert. 2 km 30 m = ☐ m
items.e: 2 km = 2,000 m. Add the 30 m: 2,000 + 30 = 2,030 m. The 3 goes in the tens place, not the hundreds.

items.q: Which is the same as 450 cm?
items.e: 100 cm = 1 m, so 400 cm = 4 m. 450 cm = 4 m and 50 cm left over.

items.q: Which is the same as 5,600 m?
items.e: 1,000 m = 1 km, so 5,000 m = 5 km. 5,600 m = 5 km and 600 m left over.

sets.title: Mass and capacity: g, kg, ml and l

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 kg = 1,000 g.

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 l = 1,000 ml.

items.q: About what is the mass of a bag of sugar?
items.e: A bag of sugar is about 1 kilogram (1,000 g). 1 g is about the mass of a paper clip.

items.q: About how much does a teaspoon hold?
items.e: A teaspoon holds about 5 millilitres. 500 ml is about a big bottle of water.

items.q: About how much does a can of fizzy drink hold?
items.e: A can of drink holds about 330 millilitres, which is about one third of a litre.

items.q: Convert. 5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need more grams: multiply. 5 × 1,000 = 5,000, so 5 kg = 5,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 6 l = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so you need more millilitres: multiply. 6 × 1,000 = 6,000, so 6 l = 6,000 ml.

items.q: Convert. 3,000 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need fewer kilograms: divide. 3,000 ÷ 1,000 = 3, so 3,000 g = 3 kg.

items.q: Convert. 7,000 ml = ☐ l
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so you need fewer litres: divide. 7,000 ÷ 1,000 = 7, so 7,000 ml = 7 l.

items.q: Convert. 2 kg 300 g = ☐ g
Convert. 2 kg 30 g = ☐ g
items.e: 2 kg = 2,000 g. Add the 30 g: 2,000 + 30 = 2,030 g. Writing 230 g forgets that 2 kg is 2,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 1 l 750 ml = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Add the 750 ml: 1,000 + 750 = 1,750 ml. 850 ml would mean 1 l = 100 ml, which is wrong.

items.q: Which is the same as 3,450 g?
items.e: 1,000 g = 1 kg, so 3,000 g = 3 kg. 3,450 g = 3 kg and 450 g left over.

items.q: Which is the same as 4,080 ml?
items.e: 4,000 ml = 4 l. 4,080 ml = 4 l and 80 ml left over (not 800 ml: the 8 is in the tens place).
The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600 g: 600 + 50 = 650 g.
Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 5 = 200 g. The needle is 2 marks past 2 kg: 2,000 + 400 = 2,400 g, which is 2 kg 400 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 equal spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 7 marks past 1 kg: 1,000 + 700 = 1,700 g, which is 1 kg 700 g.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 ml. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 ml. The water is 1 line above 600 ml: 600 + 100 = 700 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 ml. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 ml. The water is 3 lines above 250 ml: 250 + 150 = 400 ml.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres and millilitres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 ml. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 ml. The water is 3 lines above 1,000 ml: 1,000 + 300 = 1,300 ml. 1,000 ml = 1 l, so 1,300 ml = 1 l 300 ml.

items.q: Convert. 3 hours = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes (not 100). Multiply: 3 × 60 = 180, so 3 hours = 180 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 4 minutes = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Multiply: 4 × 60 = 240, so 4 minutes = 240 seconds.

items.q: Convert. 9 minutes = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Multiply: 9 × 60 = 540, so 9 minutes = 540 seconds.

items.q: Convert. 300 seconds = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Seconds to minutes: divide. 300 ÷ 60 = 5, because 5 × 60 = 300.

items.q: Convert. 240 minutes = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Minutes to hours: divide. 240 ÷ 60 = 4, because 4 × 60 = 240. 2 hours 40 minutes would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 3 years = ☐ months
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. Multiply: 3 × 12 = 36, so 3 years = 36 months.

items.q: Convert. 60 months = ☐ years
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. Months to years: divide. 60 ÷ 12 = 5, because 5 × 12 = 60.

items.q: Convert. 5 weeks = ☐ days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Multiply: 5 × 7 = 35, so 5 weeks = 35 days.

items.q: Convert. 28 days = ☐ weeks
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Days to weeks: divide. 28 ÷ 7 = 4, so 28 days = 4 weeks.

items.q: Convert. 2 days = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. Multiply: 2 × 24 = 48, so 2 days = 48 hours.

items.q: How many days are in 1 year (not a leap year)?
items.e: A year has 365 days. A leap year has one extra day, 29 February, so it has 366 days. 52 is the number of weeks in a year.

items.q: About how many weeks are in 1 year?
items.e: A year has 365 days. 365 ÷ 7 is 52 with 1 day left over, so a year is about 52 weeks. 12 is the number of months.

items.q: Convert. 2 hours 15 minutes = ☐ minutes
items.e: 2 hours = 2 × 60 = 120 minutes. Add the 15 minutes: 120 + 15 = 135 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 1 hour 40 minutes = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Add the 40 minutes: 60 + 40 = 100 minutes. 140 would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 3 minutes 20 seconds = ☐ seconds
items.e: 3 minutes = 3 × 60 = 180 seconds. Add the 20 seconds: 180 + 20 = 200 seconds.

items.q: Convert. 2 years 5 months = ☐ months
items.e: 2 years = 2 × 12 = 24 months. Add the 5 months: 24 + 5 = 29 months.

items.q: Convert. 3 weeks 2 days = ☐ days
items.e: 3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days. Add the 2 days: 21 + 2 = 23 days.

items.q: Which is the same as 150 minutes?
items.e: 120 minutes = 2 hours. 150 − 120 = 30, so 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. 1 hour 50 minutes would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.

items.q: Which is the same as 100 seconds?
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds (not 100). 100 − 60 = 40, so 100 seconds = 1 minute 40 seconds.

items.q: Which is the same as 30 months?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months, so 2 years = 24 months. 30 − 24 = 6, so 30 months = 2 years 6 months. 3 years would mean 1 year = 10 months.

items.q: How many metres are in 12 km?
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Half of 1,000 is 500, so 12 km = 500 m. 50 m would mean 1 km = 100 m.

items.q: How many grams are in 14 kg?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. To find a quarter, divide by 4: 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g.

items.q: How many millilitres are in 34 l?
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. One quarter is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 ml, so three quarters is 3 × 250 = 750 ml.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 l = ☐ ml
Convert. 2.5 km = ☐ m
items.e: 2 km = 2,000 m, and 0.5 km is half a kilometre = 500 m. 2,000 + 500 = 2,500 m.

items.q: Convert. 4.2 kg = ☐ g
How many minutes are in 12 hour?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30. 50 would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.

items.q: How many minutes are in 34 hour?
items.e: A quarter of 60 is 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so three quarters is 3 × 15 = 45 minutes.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to metres: 1 km 50 m = 1,050 m, 1 km 250 m = 1,250 m. In order: 1,250 m, 1,200 m, 1,050 m, 1,025 m. So the answer is 1 km 250 m.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 2 kg = 2,000 g, 2 kg 75 g = 2,075 g. In order: 2,075 g, 2,070 g, 2,000 g, 1,950 g. So the answer is 2 kg 75 g.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 1 l = 1,000 ml, 1 l 50 ml = 1,050 ml. In order: 1,100 ml, 1,050 ml, 1,000 ml, 900 ml. So the answer is 1,100 ml.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: Change them all to millimetres: 5 cm = 50 mm, 4 cm 5 mm = 45 mm. In order: 45 mm, 48 mm, 50 mm, 52 mm. So the answer is 4 cm 5 mm.

items.q: Which is the longest time?
items.e: Change them all to minutes: 2 hours = 120 minutes, 1 hour 50 minutes = 110 minutes. In order: 130 minutes, 120 minutes, 110 minutes, 100 minutes. So the answer is 130 minutes.

items.q: Which is the shortest time?
items.e: Change them all to seconds: 1 minute = 60 seconds, 1 minute 5 seconds = 65 seconds. In order: 58 seconds, 60 seconds, 65 seconds, 75 seconds. So the answer is 58 seconds.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m, so 3 km = 3,000 m, and 3,000 > 2,900. 2 km = 2,000 m, which is more than 1,950 m.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 hours = 120 minutes. 3 hours = 180 minutes, and 1 hour 30 minutes = 90 minutes.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 5 kg = 5,000 g, so 5 kg 60 g = 5,000 + 60 = 5,060 g. 4 kg = 4,000 g, which is less than 4,100 g.

items.q: Which list goes from the lightest to the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg 50 g = 1,050 g and 1 kg 400 g = 1,400 g. 1,050 < 1,400 < 1,500.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest to the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 2 m 5 cm = 205 cm and 2 m 30 cm = 230 cm. 205 < 230 < 250.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 km = 750 m + ☐ m
Arjun walks 1 km 200 m to school in the morning. He walks the same way home after school. How far does he walk altogether?
Maya is baking a cake. The recipe needs 350 g of flour. She has a 1 kg bag of flour. How much flour is left after baking?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Subtract: 1,000 − 350 = 650 g. Take care when you exchange: the answer is not 750 g.

items.q: A film is 130 minutes long. How long is it in hours and minutes?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 hours = 120 minutes. 130 − 120 = 10, so it is 2 hours 10 minutes. 1 hour 30 minutes would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.

items.q: Zara swims 50 lengths of a 25 m pool in a sponsored swim. How far does she swim?
Grace's sponsor gives 50p for every 100 m she swims. She swims 1 km. How much money does the sponsor give?
A sponsored walk is 5 km long. It has 4 equal stages. How long is each stage in metres?
items.e: 5 km = 5,000 m. Share it into 4 equal parts: 5,000 ÷ 4 = 1,250 m.

items.q: A bottle holds 2 litres of squash. Six cups of 250 ml are poured from it. How much squash is left?
Leo is 8 years 7 months old. How old is he in months?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months, so 8 years = 8 × 12 = 96 months. Add the 7 months: 96 + 7 = 103 months.

items.q: The summer holiday is 6 weeks long. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 6 × 7 = 42 days.

items.q: In PE, Alfie holds a plank for 2 minutes 15 seconds. How many seconds is that?
items.e: 2 minutes = 2 × 60 = 120 seconds. Add 15: 120 + 15 = 135 seconds.

items.q: In the Multiplication Tables Check there are 25 questions. Pupils get 6 seconds for each one. How long is that altogether?
items.e: 25 × 6 = 150 seconds. 120 seconds = 2 minutes, and 150 − 120 = 30, so it is 2 minutes 30 seconds.

items.q: A football match has two halves of 45 minutes and a 15-minute break at half-time. How long is that altogether?
items.e: 45 + 45 + 15 = 105 minutes. 60 minutes = 1 hour, and 105 − 60 = 45, so it is 1 hour 45 minutes.

items.q: On a school trip, the coach journey to the zoo takes 2 hours 20 minutes. The journey home takes 155 minutes. How much longer is the journey home?
items.e: 2 hours 20 minutes = 120 + 20 = 140 minutes. 155 − 140 = 15 minutes longer. 65 would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.

items.q: Aisha's school bag with books in it weighs 3 kg 200 g. The books weigh 1 kg 750 g. How much does the empty bag weigh?
items.e: Change to grams: 3,200 g − 1,750 g = 1,450 g. (1,550 g comes from taking 200 from 750 by mistake.)

items.q: How many 250 g bags of sweets weigh the same as 2 kg?
items.e: 2 kg = 2,000 g. 4 bags of 250 g make 1,000 g, so 2,000 g is 8 bags. Check: 8 × 250 = 2,000.

items.q: Kai cycles 2.5 km. Ava cycles 2,300 m. Who cycles further, and by how much?
Lily has 3 m of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces 25 cm long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: 3 m = 300 cm. 300 ÷ 25 = 12, because 4 pieces make 1 m and 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: A running track is 400 m long. How many laps make 2 km?
Freya wants to drink 1.5 litres of water today. So far she has drunk 4 glasses of 300 ml. How much more does she need to drink?
A bag of potatoes weighs 2.5 kg. Dad buys 3 bags. How much do they weigh altogether?
